There is no single market price for a Philippine green card. There are three, for a print, for correct stock, and for a number that resolves at the Bureau of Immigration. Adverts blur all three into one figure.

A green card is the United States permanent resident card. Outside the United States the same job is done by a permanent residence card, and sellers use the American term loosely for every country.

Buy a Green Card via Telegram: how the transaction works

Most Philippine green card sellers work through a channel that posts stock and a chat that closes the sale. The channel is marketing. The chat is where you find out whether the person knows the document.

Keep the photos the seller sends. When the parcel arrives, photograph the unopened envelope before you open it, then the document beside the envelope. That sequence ties the document to the seller.

Who actually issues a Green Card

The Philippine green card is a state product made by the Bureau of Immigration. Replicas copy the look, registered originals carry a number in the office records, and both are sold on Telegram as if they were the same thing.

Number formats are the one part of this that a buyer can always test without equipment. Look up the format for the Philippines and compare digit by digit. It takes a minute and settles most arguments.

Replica or registered original

If the card only has to look right across a counter, a print is enough and the bottom of the band is fair. If a number has to be looked up, pay the top and make the seller prove the lookup first.

This is the single most useful distinction on the page, because it explains the price spread better than anything else. A quote tells you which tier the seller thinks you are in.

What a fair price looks like

Price is the easiest thing to compare and the least informative. Two adverts at the same figure can differ completely in stock, number and delivery, and the figure shows you none of it.

The table below splits the band into the three tiers so you can see what each figure is actually for. Read it before you open a chat and you will not anchor on whatever number the seller opens with.

The buying process, step by step

The steps below are deliberately boring. Boring is what a Philippine green card purchase should feel like.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is the Bureau of Immigration.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format the Bureau of Immigration uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 10000–34000 PHP band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

These are the tests that matter for a Philippine green card. The two local ones are worth memorising.

  • Check the licence for the LTO regional code and the security foil on the card.
  • Confirm the passport eagle printing and the machine-readable zone.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for the Bureau of Immigration. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

Any one of these is enough to walk away. Two together is a pattern.

  • A licence where the LTO regional code does not match the address.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

What does a green card cost on Telegram?

Between 350 and 1600 US dollars. The top of the band is where a number that resolves at the immigration office should sit.

Is a green card the same as a residence permit?

In the United States yes, in practice. Elsewhere the green card is the permanent tier and the residence permit is the fixed term tier below it.

Can the number be checked?

Only against the immigration register. Ask the seller which register the number sits in and expect a specific answer.

Why are green cards so expensive?

Because the number carries the most weight of any document here and the register check is the hardest to fake.

What is the usual fake?

A high quality print of a real card with the number left intact and the personal details changed.

Before you pay

The band for a Philippine green card in the Philippines is 10000–34000 PHP. Anything else needs a reason, so ask for it.
